hypotheses.text: Complete anterior pituitary aplasia preferentially segregates with biallelic frameshift/nonsense null variants in TBC1D32, whereas structural pituitary hypoplasia with preserved residual anterior tissue predominates in individuals harboring splice-site or hypomorphic in-frame deletions.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying whether the degree of structural pituitary hypoplasia vs. complete aplasia is variant-dependent helps resolve conflicting penetrance and severity estimates between classical lethal/severe presentations and milder syndromic hypopituitarism.

evidence.text: Finnish siblings carrying compound heterozygous frameshift variants (c.1165_1166dup and c.2151del) exhibited complete absence of the anterior pituitary and panhypopituitarism, whereas a Pakistani proband with an in-frame skipping splice-site mutation (c.1372+1G>A p.Arg411_Gly458del) exhibited anterior pituitary hypoplasia rather than complete aplasia.

hypotheses.text: The structural neuroimaging hallmark of TBC1D32 deficiency is pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS triad: ectopic posterior pituitary, absent/attenuated pituitary stalk, and anterior pituitary hypoplasia/aplasia), which occurs in over 85% of live-born individuals with biallelic variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Determining whether the structural defect consistently manifests as ectopic neurohypophysis with stalk disruption (PSIS) rather than isolated hypoplasia clarifies the developmental embryopathy (Rathke pouch vs. infundibular neuroectoderm) driven by TBC1D32 ciliary dysfunction.

evidence.text: In a large congenital hypopituitarism exome cohort, pathogenic TBC1D32 variation presented with the classic triad of a hypoplastic anterior pituitary, an interrupted stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary.

hypotheses.text: True structural pituitary aplasia or hypoplasia has a penetrance of 100% in postnatal survivors with Alsahan-Harris syndrome / TBC1D32 mutations, and instances of reported 'normal' pituitary morphology represent low-resolution imaging artifacts rather than genuine organ preservation.
hypotheses.rationale: High-resolution 3T sellar MRI and thin T1-weighted sagittal sequences are necessary to detect micro-adenohypophyseal tissue and ectopic neurohypophyseal bright spots. Testing if penetrance is strictly complete eliminates phenocopies and guides diagnostic criteria.

evidence.text: TBC1D32 is expressed directly in human fetal Rathke's pouch and the developing hypothalamus during embryonic development, providing a developmental basis for obligatory structural disruption of the gland.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of confirmed TBC1D32 cases exhibit diabetes insipidus secondary to posterior pituitary dysfunction or ectopic neurohypophysis compared to isolated anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies?
new_directions.rationale: While anterior hypopituitarism is well established in ALHAS, the functional integrity of an ectopic or absent neurohypophysis bright spot on endocrine testing (arginine vasopressin secretion/water deprivation) remains insufficiently quantified.

new_directions.question_text: How consistently do lethal prenatal presentations of biallelic TBC1D32 mutations display microdissected or histological Rathke's pouch failure versus intact embryonic sella turcica?
new_directions.rationale: Fetal terminations often report external malformations (e.g. cleft lip, polydactyly, malrotation) but pituitary gland histology is rarely documented, leaving the prenatal penetrance of pituitary aplasia uncertain.
